plan.question: Can a bounded, dtype-aware trace be made compatible with the actual authorized inputs without perturbing the inherited computation, so that a later admitted same-source replay can distinguish initialization/input differences from later gradient/optimizer trajectory divergence? The concrete limitation is unresolved execution fidelity: r0017-half_total_magnitude reports validation AUC 0.6152795936767026, but its byte-identical source/config seed42 replay r0019-exact17_replay reports 0.6149279138846995, while the unchanged-gradient control reproduces AUC 0.6151021885074872 across earlier scaffolds. The four r0021 tracing attempts all fail with RuntimeError('Trace v1 supports float32/64 only; preserve failure') and export neither trace nor validation. This is a diagnostic execution failure, not counterevidence against the training mechanism. Retrieve the original failure analysis and prior replay evidence before proposing a repair. First identify the offending component/dtype through an authorized bounded diagnostic; integer IDs, boolean masks and other unsupported representations remain alternative hypotheses. Any later repair must preserve exact discrete identities, floating values, the frozen information/protocol boundary and the original failure records, then pass a trace-disabled/common-state comparison before full replay. No model edits, training or withheld assessment are authorized in this query phase.
